label: Q5 answer — the three proposed checks extend two existing validators and reuse one existing resolver, with no new script: the scenario options and expected-answer checks belong in validate-playbook-package.cjs beside requiredContentChecks (host marker at :248, REQUIRED_COMMAND_SEQUENCE at :254, per-scenario entry validateScenario at :662, fleet walk at :689) which is already the fleet-wide strict CI gate (playbook-operator-contract.yml :61, JSON fleet scan :69); the catalog anchor check belongs in validate_catalog_package.py where the raw cell still arrives intact from _extract_checkable_path (:561) and only :593 strips the :line suffix, bounds-checkable locally or resolvable through cite-drift-scan.mjs resolveCitation (:374); check-source-tags-helper.mjs classify (:282) is the strict-consumer template and validate_document.py (:1843) already shells the scanner per document.

The catalog validator already cross-checks a document against a code-owned registry — workflowMode parity requires both live sk-doc inventories to equal the key set projected by mode-registry.json (docstring :23, function :787, registry read :792, mismatch message :869) — so the anchor check is the same architecture the file already follows, and the agent-step mode check needs no new registry.

Expected-line normalization calibration — producer-side shell interpolation/format segments ($var, ${...}, $((...)), %0Nd/%Nd/%s, $$/$!, command substitution) and expected-side materialized dynamics (quoted slug values, digit runs, bracketed numbers, /tmp paths, timestamps) both map to wildcards, then full-line template equality; the live exemplar (Expected at scenario lines 90-92 stops at 'literal slugs.' while create.sh:1637 emits 'literal slugs describing the concrete work.' and the same document's Evidence at line 119 shows the full phrase) shows a strict-prefix relation must be its own failing class (EXPECTED_TRUNCATED), never a pass; a deliberate abbreviation passes only with an explicit ellipsis marker; scope is lines inside ### Expected blocks that match an emitted fragment template.

CI and test surface asymmetry, measured — playbook-operator-contract.yml runs on PR/push/schedule deliberately without path filters and executes validate-playbook-package.cjs --strict over the fleet (:61, JSON scan :69), so extending that validator inherits enforcement; no workflow references validate_catalog_package.py or its fixture test, and sk-doc-script-tests.yml's runner (:50, :53) loops only its own directory's test_*.py where the catalog-named tests exercise validate_document.py; .opencode/skills is a symlink to ../.skilled/skills, so CI's path and the edited path are one tree.

Both host validators ship fixture-based tests beside them (validate-playbook-package.test.cjs imports validatePackage; test_validator_fixtures.py imports the validator's individual check functions and copies fixtures), so each new check function has a natural test home without a new harness, and nothing in the lightest package needs a new registry or executable: every check is a pure function over files the validators already read.

direction: Edit cite-drift-scan.mjs to host the lightest checks
reason: Its resolver and its sentence/claim citation fields are already exported; adding check logic there widens the blast radius without buying anything, while the two validators already own the document-processing loops the checks need.
